nora: Heads-up: found a goroutine leak in the Go generator sample when canceling via ctx. Repro is simple: start generator, cancel after first token, then run pprof and you see a goroutine stuck in generator.go:handshakeLoop waiting on ackCh.

ben: thanks, i can repro locally. snippet i used: 
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
iter := client.Generator(ctx, req)
go func() { time.Sleep(40 * time.Millisecond); cancel() }()
for iter.Next() { _ = iter.Token() }
log.Println("iter err:", iter.Err())
```
after cancel the iterator stops yielding but a handshake reader goroutine remains.

ashwin: seems like the handshake reader isn't selecting on ctx.Done() or the writer never closes ackCh on early cancel. quick fix ideas?

mira: ergonomics note: making the iterator implement io.Closer would let samples use `defer iter.Close()` which is idiomatic. but runtime should still clean up automatically on ctx cancel so users don't have to always remember Close.

ben: plan: add an internal watcher goroutine on iterator creation that waits on ctx.Done() and calls an idempotent cleanup (sync.Once) which closes ackCh safely. Also implement io.Closer on iterator and add a ForEach(ctx, fn) convenience method for onboarding that hides Next/Err boilerplate and performs deterministic cleanup.

ashwin: prefer the writer to own closing ackCh; signal the writer to stop on ctx.Done() and have it perform the close. sync.Once can guard against races. also we need to ensure Dedicated and Private adapters use the same shared handshake helper so bug doesn't exist in those paths.

nora: samples: update the repo quickstart to show two patterns: 1) the simple ForEach example for newcomers; 2) the manual Next/Token/Err with `defer iter.Close()` for advanced users. docs should explain cancellation semantics and link to the issue/PR.

ben: i'll open a draft PR implementing: - iterator implements io.Closer - internal ctx watcher with sync.Once cleanup - ForEach(ctx, fn(ctx, Token) error) helper - unit test to assert ackCh closed exactly once - integration test that cancels after first token and asserts goroutine count returns to baseline within 200ms (integration marked to skip race detector).

mira: good. ForEach signature should take context and allow returning an error to early-stop. also include a small example in godoc and quickstart page.

dev-bot: Issue created #371: "go-sdk: generator handshake goroutine leak on ctx cancel"  https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/issues/371. Milestone: v0.14.2.

ashwin: i'll audit Dedicated/Private runtime handshake adapters once PR is up. we should add the audit to the PR checklist so reviewers confirm there are no duplicate handshake implementations.

nora: thanks all. once PR merges i'll update the sample app and onboarding docs. ping here when ready and i'll close the issue. :rocket:
